Clicking map-marker-mumbai, map-marker-bhiwandi, and map-marker-kolkata each correctly activates ONLY the matching office-card (navy gradient / text-white state). critical_code_review_comments: Presence.jsx: only the tiny solid dot (r=6/8, ~18px) is now pointer-enabled — the label text and pulse-ring correctly have pointerEvents='none'. Consider adding a small transparent <circle r=14> hitbox (pointer-events:auto) centered on each dot to enlarge the click target to ~28px for better human ergonomics, without re-introducing overlap between Mumbai & Bhiwandi. Right now real users can also click the office card on the right (which works), so this is a minor UX polish, not a blocker.
server.py: /api/contact still lacks rate-limit/captcha (carried over from iter 2 comments) — recommend adding slowapi or Turnstile before public launch to prevent MS Graph email abuse.
seed_data_creation: One additional MS Graph email was sent to it.support@vegithglobal.com as part of the contact-form regression (payload marked 'QA Iter3 Retest').
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration-3 retest of Presence map is DONE and PASSING. The fix in Presence.jsx (leader line + pointerEvents:none on halo/text) works correctly. If future testing needs to click the SVG map markers via Playwright, do NOT use element.click() with force=True on the <g data-testid='map-marker-*'> — that clicks the geometric bbox center which now lands on the pointer-events:none label. Instead: find the solid dot circle (the child <circle> with stroke='#0b1d3a') via querySelector, take getBoundingClientRect(), and use page.mouse.click(center.x, center.y). Alternatively click the office-card-<city> which also toggles the active state and is much easier to target.
rca_of_the_issue: Iter-2 issue was that Mumbai and Bhiwandi marker <g> bboxes overlapped, so the topmost <g> (Bhiwandi) captured all clicks. Iter-3 fix: (a) moved Bhiwandi marker position from ~(110,290) to (175,258) so the dots no longer overlap; (b) added an anchor dot + dashed leader line back to the real coord so the geographic accuracy is preserved; (c) set pointerEvents:'none' on the pulse-halo <circle> and label <text> so ONLY the tiny inner dot receives clicks — this prevents the wide label boxes from stealing pointer events from adjacent markers. Verified end-to-end with click at dot coords: mumbai/bhiwandi/kolkata each activate the correct office card independently.
